definition: A silhouette that is closer at the top and opens gradually toward the hem. The same outline can appear on tunics, dresses, skirts, and jackets.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a simple belt at the waist; leaving it unmarked is also fine.
A fitted layer over the top can sit under a more open hem if you want contrast.
These are pairing ideas, not a required outline.
comfort_notes: A lighter lining and a hem that does not cling can feel easier in warm rooms. Comfort still depends on fabric and personal preference.

definition: A tailored jacket that can be worn open or closed. It is not limited by gender and can sit over many kinds of tops.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a collared shirt; a knit top is another option.
Straight trousers or a long tunic can both sit under the same jacket.
These combinations are suggestions, not a dress code.
weather_notes: Unlined or lightweight cloth is often easier in heat. Comfort still depends on fabric weight, construction, and preference.

definition: Cloth that lets air and moisture move more readily than a dense, coated weave. Breathability is a material quality, not a promise of comfort for every climate.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a loose top in an open weave over a closer layer.
A breathable lining can sit under a heavier outer cloth.
Choose the weave you prefer; this is not a rule.
weather_notes: Open weaves can feel easier in humidity, but wind and personal preference still matter. They are not a guarantee of coolness.

definition: Placing two or more distinct colour fields next to each other rather than blending them. The effect can be quiet or high-contrast depending on the colours you choose.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a solid top against a solid bottom in a different hue.
A third colour in shoes or a scarf can stay smaller if you want the two main fields to lead.
These are suggestions, not a required palette.
comfort_notes: Choosing colours you already like to wear can feel easier than forcing a high-contrast pair. Preference leads here.

definition: Dressing for a celebration by choosing cloth, colour, or ornament you associate with the occasion. Festive does not require a particular garment or a formal dress code.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a usual everyday silhouette in a richer cloth.
A small piece of jewellery or a brighter dupatta can mark the occasion without changing the whole outfit.
These are ideas, not rules for any festival.
comfort_notes: If you expect to stand or sit for a long time, a familiar fit and a breathable cloth can feel easier. Comfort is personal.

definition: A tunic-length top with a straight or slightly shaped body and a front opening or placket. People of any gender wear kurtas for everyday and celebration.
cultural_context: Worn across South Asia in cotton, silk, and mixed fibres.
pairing_suggestions: One option is straight trousers; palazzo pants or jeans are other options.
A light shawl or jacket can sit over the same kurta in cooler rooms.
These pairings are suggestions, not a required set.
weather_notes: Lighter cotton is often easier in heat. Comfort still depends on fabric weight, fit, and preference.

definition: Wearing more than one garment so that edges, lengths, or textures show in combination. Layers can be added or removed as the room or weather changes.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a close top under an open jacket or shawl.
A longer kurta over slim trousers can read as two layers without extra bulk.
These are suggestions, not a stacking rule.
weather_notes: Thin inner layers are often easier to add or remove when indoor and outdoor temperatures differ. This is not a guarantee of warmth.

definition: A gathered or paneled skirt, often worn with a separate top and an optional drape. It is not limited by gender and can be made in many lengths and weights.
cultural_context: Common at South Asian celebrations, with many regional cuts and names.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a fitted or straight blouse; a kurta-length top is another option.
A dupatta can be draped, left off, or replaced with a jacket.
These are suggestions, not a required three-piece set.
comfort_notes: A lighter inner cloth and a waist that you can sit in can feel easier over a long event. Choose the weight and drawstring you prefer.

definition: A plant-fibre cloth that wrinkles readily and lets air through more than many dense weaves. Linen appears in shirts, kurtas, trousers, and home textiles.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a linen shirt with cotton trousers so both layers stay relatively open.
A linen kurta can sit over a closer knit if you want a second layer.
These are suggestions, not a required fibre mix.
weather_notes: Linen often feels easier in dry heat; in damp air it can cling. Comfort still depends on weave, finish, and preference.

definition: Dressing in one colour family from top to bottom, including close tints and shades of that colour. It is a styling choice, not a requirement for formality.
pairing_suggestions: One option is matching a top and bottom in the same hue with a slightly different texture.
Shoes or a belt in a nearby shade can stay inside the family without matching exactly.
These are ideas, not a uniform.
comfort_notes: Staying with a colour you already wear often can feel easier than introducing a new palette. Preference leads here.

definition: A cut that leaves space between the cloth and the body rather than following every contour. Relaxed is a fit description, not a judgment of shape.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a relaxed top with a straighter lower garment if you want contrast.
Two relaxed pieces can also be worn together.
These are suggestions, not a required balance.
comfort_notes: Extra ease can feel helpful in heat or during long sitting. How much ease you want is personal.

definition: A way of wrapping a long unstitched length of cloth around the body, with many regional methods. No single drape is the only correct one.
cultural_context: Draping methods vary widely across South Asia and in diaspora practice.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a stitched blouse; a close knit or a shirt can also sit under the drape.
The free end can rest over a shoulder, a belt, or a jacket.
These are suggestions, not a required drape.
comfort_notes: A drape you already know how to walk and sit in can feel easier than a new wrap on a long day. Comfort depends on cloth, tuck, and preference.

definition: A smooth animal-fibre cloth with a slight sheen. Weight ranges from airy to dense, so silk is not automatically warm or cool.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a silk top with a matte cotton or linen lower garment.
A silk dupatta can sit over a simpler everyday outfit.
These are suggestions, not a required mix of sheen.
weather_notes: Lightweight silk can feel easier in mild weather; heavier silk holds more warmth. Comfort still depends on lining, weave, and preference.

definition: A mix of informal pieces with one more considered item, such as a jacket, a leather shoe, or a pressed cloth. It is a loose description, not a fixed uniform.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a blazer over a simple knit and trousers.
A kurta with tailored pants can read in the same range.
These are suggestions, not an office rule.
comfort_notes: Keeping one familiar comfortable piece in the mix can feel easier than changing every layer. Preference still leads.

definition: A long, belted outer coat with a collar and often a storm flap. It can be worn by people of any gender over many outfits.
pairing_suggestions: One option is a simple top and trousers so the coat stays the outer layer.
A kurta or long tunic can sit underneath if the coat has enough ease.
These are suggestions, not a required inner outfit.
weather_notes: A water-resistant finish can help in light rain; it is not a guarantee in heavy weather. Comfort still depends on lining, length, and preference.
